searches.note: Twenty eight searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's: one shared on the Amarone rules (the December pressing rule and the DOCG decree of 24 March 2010) serves Quintarelli and Bertani. Seven were restricted to a primary body's or a house's own domain (bertani.net with library.bertani.net once, masi.it twice, pieropan.it once, prosecco.it once, bisol.it twice) and are read as primary through their summaries. One WebFetch was tried, on www.masi.it, refused by the network (the host does not resolve here) and never retried. The allowance ran out with every record tested; nothing that rests on no source was kept.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification and its year, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the facts that matter most: the dates and the people, the classifications, the sites and the making; a fact the Codex library states stood on the library unless a search contradicted it.

Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a claim rested on one account only it was softened or cut, since an empty field is a true answer; where the author's primary source holds a fact the refuter could not reach again, it stands and is listed as open.
Sources whose address carries a writer's or an importer's personal name (a wine wiki under a first name, an importer's shop under its founder's name) were read in the results but never cited.

tested: The founder and the move: Callmewine and Enoteca Properzio both have the founder, with his brothers, sharecropping at Figari in Marano di Valpolicella and moving to Cerè, Negrar, in 1924: confirmed. GuildSomm's profile gives 1906 as the year established, so founded stays empty as the library has it.

Bepi: born 1927 and the youngest son (Enoteca Properzio, Callmewine); Decanter's obituary has him dead at eighty four in January 2012 and taking over in 1950, a merchant the early 1950s: confirmed as around 1950; the dates 1927 to 2012 stand.

The blend: Callmewine, Superiore.de and Corney and Barrow give Corvina and Corvinone, Rondinella and a small share of Cabernet, Nebbiolo, Croatina and Sangiovese: confirmed, and the question's key with it.
The cask: about seven years in large Slavonian oak by Callmewine, Superiore.de and a producer profile: confirmed.
Rosso del Bepi: Lea and Sandeman, FRW and Nick's give 2008 as a year with no Amarone and Rosso del Bepi instead, Nick's and others 2010: confirmed.
The labels: merchants and a producer profile describe hand written labels, drawn and glued by hand; no obituary read says Bepi did it himself: changed.

Alzero: Wine Library, K and L and Callmewine give Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Merlot, about two fifths, two fifths and one fifth, labelled Cabernet Veneto IGT, aged in French oak; one merchant calls an older vintage mostly Cabernet Franc: changed from Cabernet Franc alone.
Monte Ca' Paletta: Vinexus and Enoteca Properzio place the estate at Cerè on Ca' Paletta; only one profile calls its vines the oldest: the site stands, the oldest is cut.

The December rule: the DOCG's rules bar pressing before 1 December in a normal year (Vinetur, an Italian guide, the disciplinare copies on certifico.com); the Veneto Region allowed an earlier start on 5 November 2025 and 2 November 2026 at the consorzio's request: hedged.

The rules of the house: nobody living named (the daughter, her husband, the grandson and the cellar master are met in the obituaries and kept out); no price, score or volatile figure; British spelling; no dash.

tested: The founding: Giovan Battista and Gaetano Bertani, brothers, at Quinto di Valpantena in 1857 (Callmewine, the Italian Botanical Heritage page, Great Wine): confirmed; their dates not found, so they stay described.
Guyot: Great Wine and a second account have Gaetano trained by, and the friend of, Jules Guyot in Burgundy: confirmed as the house's story, hedged.
The royal warrant of 1923: the house's library site gives 1923 and the Kingdom of Italy; a second account says the early 1920s: stands as the house's own claim, hedged.
The coronation of 1937: Soave Bertani served at the coronation of George VI by two accounts; none names a lunch: changed.

1958 at Tenuta Novare: the house's library site and its Italian news page give 1958 as the first official vintage; Enotria and Decanter have Novare bought at the end of the Second World War: confirmed.

The cask: seven years in Slavonian oak of fifty to one hundred hectolitres on the house's product page; at least eight months in bottle after; other accounts six to eight years: at least seven stands.
Concrete: Decanter twice and Terroir Amarone have fermentation in concrete (cement) vats for about a month to fifty days; a Drinks Business masterclass report has steel: stands, listed as open.
The blend: the house's sheet and Enotria give eighty Corvina Veronese and twenty Rondinella; a Decanter feature says Rondinella never above a tenth: softened.

The sale: WineNews and Blitz Quotidiano have the Angelini group's wine company buying majority stakes in Bertani Holding and Novare on 1 December 2011, the brand, Grezzana and Novare among them; the family's Tenuta Santa Maria pages tell the land it kept: confirmed, told as control.
The rules of the house: nobody living named; no price, score or volatile figure; the sale told as history.

tested: 1772 and the name: the house's history page has the Boscaini family's first harvest in the Vaio dei Masi in 1772 and the company named Masi in 1972, for the two hundredth year: stands as the house's account, hedged.

1964 and 1967: the house's pages give 1964 and the name Ripasso taken from the old cellar words of Valpolicella; Decanter's sponsored history and The Drinks Business give produced in 1964 and sold from 1967: confirmed.
Labelled Ripasso: Sevenfifty has the first wine named Campofiorin Ripasso; The Drinks Business has the word taken off the label around 2000; a 2001 label still carries it: stands, listed as open.
The 1980s: the house's pages give the refinement into a double fermentation with whole semi dried grapes in the 1980s, the technical group formed in the mid 1980s: confirmed.
The share of dried grapes: the house's page gives about 30 per cent, a 2016 sheet reproduced by Charton Hobbs 25: hedged as the house's figure.

The wood: the 2016 sheet gives at least eighteen months, two thirds in 90 hectolitre Slavonian casks, a third in new 600 litre barrels, then three months in bottle; the house's brochure names 600 litre barrels: stands.
Serving temperature: the house's Campofiorin page gives 18 to 20 degrees, its Nectar Campofiorin page 18: the house clause cut, the Codex's 16 to 18 kept.
Serego Alighieri: WineNews and Cayman Compass have Dante's son Pietro buying Casal dei Ronchi at Gargagnago in 1353 and Masi working with the counts since 1973: confirmed, the sentence rebuilt.
The appellation: the house's own page is titled Rosso Verona IGT, a merchant prints Rosso del Veronese IGP; the IGT carries both names: the question rekeyed.
The rules of the house: the head of the house and his son, both in people.json, are kept out; Dante and Pietro described, not named.

changed.now: In 1973 Masi began to work on the wines of the Serego Alighieri counts, descendants of the poet of the Divine Comedy, whose son bought the family's estate at Gargagnago in 1353.
changed.why: The old sentence let whose and who hang on the wines; the accounts give the purchase of Casal dei Ronchi by the poet's son in 1353.

tested: 1542: the house's story page has the first record of the family's presence in Chartice, the Cartizze of today, in 1542; Falstaff and Glass of Bubbly carry the same; a retailer gives 1875 as a start up year: the record of presence stands, the ownership since 1542 is cut, founded stays empty.

The forebear and his son: the house's page has the trade broken by the First World War, revived in the mid 1920s by the son, who after the Second World War went through the hills of Valdobbiadene and Conegliano for plots to buy: confirmed.
The law: the consorzio has the DOC of 2 April 1969 for Prosecco and Superiore di Cartizze, the subzone's own rules since 1969 and the DOCG of 2009: confirmed.
Lunelli in 2014: the house's page: confirmed.

The site: the house's terroir page has a steep crest rising to 300 metres, sunny and sheltered from cold winds, friable soil over rock; other accounts give 200 to 350 metres: changed to the house's words.

The making: no Bisol page beyond the fact sheets the author read gave the pressing, the settling, the thirty days or the malolactic; other houses' Cartizze sheets give thirty to ninety days: stands on the house's sheets, listed as open.
Relio and Crede: both on the house's own pages; Relio is named for a forebear: confirmed.
Dry: sweeter than Extra Dry and Brut on the sweetness scale the Codex teaches: confirmed.
The rules of the house: the head of the house, met in the results, kept out; the forebear and his son described.

codexInTension.says: Alzero made by appassimento from Cabernet Franc; Alzero is a dried-grape Cabernet Franc.

codexInTension.says: Quintarelli's Alzero is dried-grape Cabernet Franc and is not Amarone.

codexInTension.says: first made in 1964, the model for the modern double-fermentation style
codexInTension.against: The 1964 wine was refermented on Amarone pomace, the model for Ripasso; the double fermentation with whole semi dried grapes is the house's refinement of the 1980s, by its own pages (the author's finding, confirmed).
